comparedAgainst: web search results for 'four pillars of OOP encapsulation abstraction inheritance polymorphism C#' (Medium, DEV, c-sharpcorner, Pluralsight snippets only, not read in full)
justification: Judged fresh before opening the round-1 files. The top results for this query are one-line definitions plus analogy examples: Microsoft Learn's tutorial extends a BankAccount with inherited account types and a virtual month-end method, and freeCodeCamp uses Person/Father/Child, BankAccount, MusicPlayer and Animal/Dog with family-tree and gift-box analogies. Neither treats encapsulation as invariant protection, shows what the runtime does with a virtual call, states the cost of inheritance, or gives exercises with worked solutions; the freeCodeCamp page explicitly avoids design trade-offs and dispatch mechanics. This article adds real original value on each: a billing domain of its own; a before/after invoice with public fields versus guarded methods, with real output; an AsReadOnly leak exercise; a method-table figure tied to the Book of the Runtime plus a GetBaseDefinition reflection demo; overloading versus overriding; a delegate as polymorphism without inheritance; two runnable inheritance failure modes (virtual call from a base constructor, override breaking an unwritten postcondition) with the Template Method fix; an abstraction section arguing what an interface should admit (Unreachable). It has no filler intro or outro: the first sentence delivers, and the closing section synthesizes and argues which pillars to reach for first. Not templated: headings, openings and exercise forms (find the way in, predict, move the check, extend, reason about a call site) differ from test-doubles, sql-joins and branching-and-merging; there is no oop-design sibling yet and docs/crosslinks/oop-design/four-pillars-of-oop.md exists, is sensible and states coverage boundaries with composition-over-inheritance, solid-principles and interfaces-vs-abstract-classes, so near-duplicate risk is managed. Copy check: two distinctive sentences searched in quotes (abstraction/encapsulation framing, 'a good abstraction leaves out what varies...') returned no matching passage. Quoted material is short, attributed and inline-cited. I re-fetched the virtual stub dispatch document: it does say VSD is enabled only for interface calls and that virtual instance calls were left on a true vtable because of startup and throughput, so the :::dotnet paraphrase is faithful. The Microsoft Learn 'four basic principles' quotation matches the page I fetched. Experience claims are honest: the one measured-behavior statement (primary-constructor demo printing 12/seat on both lines) says what it was run on. Hard-rule checks: no invented statistics, anecdotes or first-person experience; Liskov, Wadler and Gamma et al. are attributed to real works; generalisations flagged in the pilot lessons were scoped (round-1 'exactly one base class' now 'can have only one', thread parenthesis now says synchronization is needed on top, CS0108 and CS8509 now cited or stated exactly). Round-1 findings, all checked against the current text: (1) level/beginner mismatch, major, largely fixed: each pillar now has a one-sentence plain definition at first use and virtual/abstract/override are glossed where the Plan program is introduced, but front matter still says level: beginner with no prerequisites while the middle of the page uses records, primary constructors, reflection and JIT devirtualization; residual minor. (2) 'X, not Y' tic, minor, fixed: the ', not ' construction no longer appears in the prose; remaining 'instead of' / 'rather than' uses are ordinary. (3) unsupported small claims, minor, mostly fixed: 'sometimes called compile-time polymorphism' clause removed, CS0108 linked and in sources, billing-latency sentence made conditional; Liskov and Wing 1994 is now named with author, title and year but still has no source entry or link, which is the one round-1 item not fully closed. (4) over-general wording, fixed. (5) question-heading density, no change required: 11 of about 17 H2/H3 headings are questions, which is the plan's Q shape; siblings use statement headings, so no site-wide tic. The page ends in an exercise and then the shell's next-step cards, so there is no navigation dead end. No policy problems: no ad code, no fabricated credentials, no copied text. What keeps it below 9.5: the beginner label, one unsourced named paper, and a sourcing weakness on Gamma et al. (the source URL is a publisher catalog page that cannot itself support the chapter claims). These are nits, not low-value-content signals.

issues.location: Front matter (level: beginner, prerequisites: []) versus 'How does polymorphism work at run time?' onward (records, primary constructors, reflection, JIT devirtualization, guarded devirtualization in the last exercise)
issues.problem: Round-1 major, mostly fixed by plain definitions at first use, but the label still promises a beginner page with no prerequisites while the second half is squarely intermediate. A reviewer or reader comparing the label with the content sees a mismatch.
issues.fixLooksLike: Set level to intermediate, or keep beginner and add a prerequisite such as classes and objects in C#, or add a one-line signpost before 'What the runtime does with plan.PriceFor(usage)' saying the section can be skipped on a first read.

issues.location: 'An override can break a promise the base class made', last paragraph: 'Barbara Liskov and Jeannette Wing's 1994 paper "A Behavioral Notion of Subtyping"'
issues.problem: Round-1 asked for a citation of the Liskov substitution principle. The paper is now named in the text but has no entry in the sources front matter and no link or inline [n] marker, so the one named-principle claim in the article is still unsourced under hard rule 3. The plan's SOLID crosslink does not substitute for it while that article is unpublished.
issues.fixLooksLike: Add the Liskov and Wing 1994 paper (ACM TOPLAS 16(6)) to sources with an accessed date and a link (the ACM DL or the CMU copy), and cite it inline after the sentence, or reword so the sentence claims only what the page opened supports.

issues.location: Sources entry 13 (Design Patterns, url pearson.com catalog page) and inline citations [13] under 'What does inheritance cost?' and the Template Method exercise solution
issues.problem: The cited URL is a publisher product page that says nothing about chapter 1's composition-versus-inheritance argument or the Template Method pattern, and the accessed date implies the page was opened. The brief allows textbook citations for well-known facts by chapter name, which the entry does, but a link that cannot support the clause can look like a citation for show.
issues.fixLooksLike: Keep the chapter names, drop the implication that the linked page is the source (for example publisher: 'Addison-Wesley, 1994; book, not opened online' or an accessed note saying it is a bibliographic pointer), or point to a library or publisher record that is clearly a bibliographic entry.
